about: Every privilege that a role other than the object's owner holds on this database, on its schemas and on their tables, columns, sequences, functions and types, and every default privilege, as packages/db/test/catalogue.integration.test.ts reads them from the migrated schema. A grant change is a diff of this file: change it in the same pull request as the migration and say why in the migration header. A column privilege is written "UPDATE (column)". Every tinnox_definer entry says in "why" which sec.* function or script uses it, and names any part that nothing uses.

function public.app_org_id().why: sec.pairing_claim, sec.pairing_cancel_claims and sec.session_revoke_membership read the caller's organisation context with it.

schema public.why: The sec.* functions name public tables and call public.app_org_id().

schema sec.why: It owns the functions in sec. Migrations create and replace them under SET LOCAL ROLE tinnox_definer, which needs CREATE on the schema.

table public.alert_recipient.why: sec.alert_recipient_by_token_hash resolves a confirmation link opened with no session: it filters on confirm_token_hash, confirmed_at and confirm_expires_at and returns org_id and id. Never email (AG-1.20).

table public.audit_event.why: sec.audit_unscoped writes events that have no organisation. scripts/revoke-all-sessions.sql, scripts/revoke-subject-sessions.sql, provision-member pending and migration 0012 write audit rows for every organisation under SET LOCAL ROLE tinnox_definer. INSERT only: audit_event is append-only.

table public.display.why: sec.pairing_claim and sec.pairing_cancel_claims check that the display belongs to the caller's organisation.

table public.heartbeat_log.why: sec.heartbeat_log_purge deletes history older than the retention in every organisation; received_at is the only column it reads.

table public.login_state.why: sec.login_state_put deletes expired rows and inserts one; sec.login_state_take deletes one and returns it (its WHERE and RETURNING need SELECT). tinnox_app has no rights on the table. UPDATE is granted (0001) and no function or script uses it: a line to drop in a new migration (SCR-27).

table public.media.why: sec.media_processing_jobs lists media still waiting for the worker in every organisation: it filters on status and returns id, org_id and created_at.

table public.member_invite.why: Script only, no sec.* function reads it (AG-1.19): under SET LOCAL ROLE tinnox_definer, provision-member pending expires old invites (UPDATE (status)) and lists the pending ones of every organisation, and provision-member fulfil finds an invite's organisation. invited_by is granted (0013) and no definer statement reads it: a line to drop in a new migration (SCR-27).

table public.membership.why: SELECT: sec.membership_by_oidc_sub, sec.session_create, sec.session_by_id_hash, sec.pairing_claim and sec.pairing_complete look a member up, and provision-member finds a member's organisation by id or subject under SET LOCAL ROLE tinnox_definer. UPDATE (first_signed_in_at): sec.session_create stamps the first sign-in, and its FOR NO KEY UPDATE lock needs UPDATE on one column. UPDATE (sessions_valid_after): sec.session_revoke_membership locks the member row (FOR NO KEY UPDATE, 0015) and sets the cut-off, also for scripts/revoke-subject-sessions.sql, which calls it; the FOR SHARE lock of sec.pairing_complete rests on it too (AG-1.18).

table public.organization.why: sec.membership_by_oidc_sub and sec.session_by_id_hash return the organisation's name, sec.display_alert_orgs lists every id for the alert check, and provision-member pending prints the organisation of each invite.

table public.pairing_claim_failure.why: sec.pairing_claim counts, records and purges an operator's wrong codes. tinnox_app has no rights on the table. UPDATE is granted (0001) and no function or script uses it: a line to drop in a new migration (SCR-27).

table public.pairing_session.why: The sec.pairing_* functions are the only way to it: pairing_create inserts, pairing_poll, pairing_claim, pairing_complete and pairing_cancel_claims read and update, pairing_purge deletes. tinnox_app has no rights on the table.

table public.player_registration.why: sec.device_by_token_hash and sec.device_by_registration_id resolve a device credential before the organisation is known; sec.pairing_complete inserts the registration; sec.pairing_claim revokes the one it replaces (revoked_at, revoked_reason).

table public.session.why: The sec.session_* functions are the only way to it: session_create inserts, session_by_id_hash, session_revoke and session_revoke_membership update, session_purge_expired updates and deletes. scripts/revoke-all-sessions.sql updates it under SET LOCAL ROLE tinnox_definer; scripts/revoke-subject-sessions.sql calls sec.session_revoke_membership (0015). tinnox_app has no rights on the table.
